sections.html: Macrognathus maculatus has a circumferential fin (dorsal, tail and anal fins joined). Size-wise, the species is in the middle range among spiny eels. The variable colored species is very nicely patterned and very peaceful.
Macrognathus maculatus originates from Indonesia and Malaysia; reports from other parts of Southeast Asia (Cambodia, Vietnam) probably refer to similar other species.
The species is very peaceful. Only very small fish should not be kept together with them: sooner or later they will end up in the stomach of the spiny eels.
The animals are fully sexually differentiated: males are much slimmer than females.

Spiny eels come in different sizes, from the only about 10 cm long Macrognathus pancalus from India to the giant spiny eel Mastacembelus armatus with up to 90 cm. The old rule of thumb that Asian spiny eels with a clearly separated caudal fin remain small no longer works after recent revisions: small species with a circumferential fin are known, as well as large ones with a separate caudal fin (e.g. Macrognathus kris from Borneo, up to 40 cm). The animals described here are 15-20 cm long; the literature gives sizes up to 28 cm.
